originalTitle: Trump engineered a risky comeback for Jensen Huang
summary: After Nvidia's board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. content: After Nvidia’s board accepted Jensen Huang’s resignation as CEO, following reports that Huang had an affair with an alleged Chinese spy, President Donald Trump, too, appeared to submit to the new reality. Appearing on Stephen A. Smith’s radio show shortly after the news came out, Trump said that Huang would “end up on his feet.” “You know the expression, anybody can be replaced,” Trump said, floating Apple’s ex-CEO Tim Cook as a potential CEO candidate. It didn’t take long for Trump to begin softening his approach, making it clear he’d welcome Huang back into the role of CEO even if Nvidia’s own board wasn’t ready to do so. Behind the scenes, the Trump administration was working to grease the landing for Huang’s return. And soon, Nvidia’s board changed its tune: Barely a week after insisting they all agreed to shut the door on Huang’s return, they voted unanimously to reinstate him as CEO, president, and board director. “There’s nothing wrong with a comeback,” Trump said in a celebratory call to CNBC. Trump then posted an image on Truth Social of Huang transposed onto Trump’s own body in the infamous photo of him raising his fist after being shot at a campaign rally. In his raised fist, Huang-on-Trump’s-body is clutching a scarlet bra, holding it high in the air. Even after a decisive blow to the president’s power as Democrats swept the midterm elections, Trump appears to maintain his position as a corporate kingmaker. Trump said he spoke with Huang the night prior to his reinstatement and had been in communication with the board both “directly and indirectly.” White House communications director Steven Cheung said in a statement that “President Trump was totally involved” in the board’s decision — Trump decided near the end of last week that he wanted to lead efforts to get Huang reappointed, per The New York Times, so he asked Vice President JD Vance to act as a liaison between Huang and Nvidia’s board, providing reassurances that the move wouldn’t pose a security risk. Trump also reportedly dialed into Nvidia’s Sunday night board meeting to make the case for his return. “I made the deal,” he told CNBC on Monday. News of Huang’s reappointment, nearly as dramatic as Sam Altman’s return to his CEO role after being voted out by OpenAI’s board in 2023, was a widespread shock to experts, analysts, and investors, particularly after Nvidia’s board had assured stakeholders on its quarterly earnings call last Tuesday that the board “does not intend to reinstate Jensen as CEO.” On Monday morning, a surge in NASDAQ-100 futures hit a circuit-breaker limit and caused a halt in trading over the volatility. Trump has meddled in other messy incidents, including by repeatedly — and perhaps illegally — extending the deadline for TikTok to complete its sale to a US entity, and, he admitted on Monday, protecting Tesla and SpaceX CEO Elon Musk. Although he said on CNBC that Musk is “80 percent super genius, 20 percent he has other problems,” Trump said it’s important to protect people like him and Huang. “We have to protect our brilliant people because we don’t have enough.” But the upcoming Democratic-majority Congress could test both Huang and Trump’s influence. As Republicans prepare for an open presidential primary in 2028, at least one potential candidate appears to be breaking with the president in their skepticism of Huang and Nvidia. And Democrats seem eager to probe both Nvidia and the Trump administration. The past couple of weeks have been tumultuous for Nvidia. Huang admitted he had had an affair with Alice Huang (no relation), a former executive at Nvidia customer Megaspeed whom some US intelligence officers reportedly believed to be a potential Chinese spy. There were nearly immediate reports of an additional affair with a direct report, as well as an alleged third affair with a second employee. Megaspeed has reportedly also been investigated for a broader attempt to illegally funnel advanced Nvidia chips to China. Huang himself has pushed to open up more chip sales to China, and he reportedly lied to the Nvidia board about his infidelity. He’s scheduled to testify before Congress on December 1st. The Nvidia board tried to address concerns about Huang in its announcement Monday, writing that members “received input from senior levels of the United States government, and based on that input, the Board is confident that Mr. Huang’s reinstatement poses no national security risk.” It made assurances that the independent investigation it had kicked off about Huang and foreign intelligence would “proceed to conclusion” with Huang’s cooperation. The board also said it had recently formed an entirely new National Security and Export Control Committee “comprised solely of independent directors to oversee trade compliance and national security risks,” which is working with legal counsel and advisers who have national security experience. Nvidia will be hiring for a new C-suite position, the board said: chief compliance officer. The executive will “oversee compliance” across the company and report to the Nominating and Corporate Governance committees. “NVIDIA will continue to cooperate with ongoing government investigations and inquiries,” the board added. Still, the reaction to Huang’s return reflects how small the chance of Huang’s return seemed before Trump’s efforts. Although Trump had previously cast doubt on multiple reports that Alice Huang was a spy, The New York Times reported on Sunday that she “kept in contact with an official of China’s top spy agency for more than a year.” According to the Times, which cited multiple people with knowledge of US intelligence reports, Kang Wei — Alice Huang’s business partner and, by some reports, husband, who reportedly introduced her to the Nvidia CEO — worked with the same Chinese intelligence agency. chineseTitle: 特朗普为黄仁勋设计了一次危险的复出
chineseSummary: 有报道称黄仁勋与一名所谓的中国间谍有染，英伟达董事会接受黄仁勋辞去首席执行官职务后，唐纳德·特朗普总统似乎也接受了新的现实。消息传出后不久，特朗普在斯蒂芬·A·史密斯的广播节目中表示，黄仁勋“最终会站起来”。 […]
chineseContent: 有报道称黄仁勋与一名所谓的中国间谍有染，英伟达董事会接受黄仁勋辞去首席执行官职务后，唐纳德·特朗普总统似乎也接受了新的现实。消息传出后不久，特朗普在斯蒂芬·A·史密斯的广播节目中表示，黄仁勋“最终会站起来”。特朗普表示：“你知道这句话，任何人都可以被取代。”他将苹果前首席执行官蒂姆·库克列为潜在的首席执行官候选人。没过多久，特朗普就开始软化他的态度，明确表示他欢迎黄仁勋重新担任首席执行官，即使英伟达自己的董事会还没有准备好这样做。在幕后，特朗普政府正在努力为黄的回归做好准备。很快，英伟达董事会就改变了态度：在坚持同意关闭黄仁勋回归的大门不到一周后，他们一致投票决定恢复黄仁勋的首席执行官、总裁和董事会董事职务。 “卷土重来并没有什么问题，”特朗普在接受 CNBC 的电话庆祝时说道。随后，特朗普在Truth Social上发布了一张黄的照片，这张照片被移植到特朗普自己的身上，这张臭名昭著的照片显示他在竞选集会上被枪击后举起拳头。黄对特朗普举起的拳头中，紧紧抓着一件猩红色的胸罩，将其高举在空中。即使在民主党在中期选举中大获全胜而对总统权力造成决定性打击之后，特朗普似乎仍保持着企业王者的地位。特朗普表示，他在黄仁勋复职前一天晚上与他进行了交谈，并与董事会进行了“直接和间接”的沟通。白宫通讯主管史蒂文·张(Steven Cheung)在一份声明中表示，“特朗普总统完全参与”了委员会的决定——特朗普在上周末附近决定，他希望领导委员会的工作。
